title: What a grantee or a relayer can do, and what holds.
caption: T2, T6 and T8 are Theorems 2, 6 and 8 of the formal results; O-labels name the obligations on the account code around the decision function, which the verification companion paper lists. The vision companion paper covers owner-key theft, guardians and the verifier registry.
rows: Sign within rules naming its key; build any invocation tree; choose among rules naming its key

T2: every call of an accepted request is allowed by an installed rule (signer authentication, selection and context conversion tested, O1, O2, O7). T6: each capped rule's window stays within its limit (selection and record persistence tested, O2, O6). T8: no grant rule allows a call to the account or its adopted recovery contracts (proved for lowering; the runtime recheck tested)

The union of authority across rules naming its key; caps per rule, not per grant; each call checked alone; allowances and `execute`; `approve` through a token rule with no function list; replacing a rule starts a new window
Wrap signed entries, choose timing and fee, resubmit a refused entry until its expiration ledger
An external signer's signature binds this account, the entry and the selected rule IDs (tested; a paper proof under signature and hash assumptions)
Delegated signers do not bind rule IDs. A rule edited in place between signing and inclusion decides under its new contents
